result.status: Done. 12/12 tests pass in tests/unit/safe-next-path.test.ts, and `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint . --max-warnings=0` both print nothing. The test was red first (module not found) and went green after the move. The old colon check was dead code: it only ran after the earlier startsWith("/") guard, so it could never fire. The old function already blocked most of the listed inputs, so the real changes are the new URL() same-origin check and moving the function into a pure module. login-form.tsx now imports safeNextPath from that module; the form behaviour is otherwise unchanged.

assumptions: The task labels the test 'R36', but SPEC.md R36 is 'server code authenticates + checks org and role itself on every endpoint'. I kept the describe name as instructed; it is only a label mismatch.

Moved the function to a pure file, src/components/app-shell/safe-next-path.ts, instead of editing in place. This keeps the 'use client' login form (React, next/navigation, supabase browser client) out of the unit test's imports. The task listed this file as allowed.

The parameter type is now `unknown` rather than `string | null | undefined`. The test passes an array (repeated ?next=) and the form passes a string, so the wider type is compatible with the existing call site.

'/%2F%2Fevil.com' is kept as-is, since nothing is decoded and it is a literal same-origin path. The task allows either that or the '/' fallback, so the test asserts it resolves to the local origin and equals one of those two values. Any later decoding by a consumer (for example a redirect that decodes first) would need its own check.

The existing rejection of any backslash anywhere in the path is kept. It is stricter than the task text, which only asks to reject a leading '/\'. This is safe for the app's own next values, but a legitimate path with a literal backslash would fall back to '/'.
No package installs and no DB access were needed.
